seoTitle: Remove Taxes on Shopify Checkout & POS
metaDescription: Learn how to disable tax calculation on Shopify checkout and POS for specific products, regions, or your entire store, with changes applying instantly.
intro: Not every Shopify store needs to charge tax, but the default setup can leave an estimated tax line showing at checkout and in POS. This guide explains how to turn off automatic tax collection for specific products, regions, or your whole store so the checkout reflects accurate pricing.

steps.heading: Navigate to tax settings
steps.body: Head to the tax settings area in Shopify Admin, which is the central place for controlling how tax is applied across your store.

steps.heading: Turn off automatic tax collection
steps.body: Disable automatic tax collection at the level that applies to you — whether that's a specific region, a set of products, or your entire store.

steps.heading: Apply changes to specific products if needed
steps.body: If only certain products shouldn't be taxed, adjust their individual tax settings rather than changing the store-wide configuration.

steps.heading: Save and confirm changes apply instantly
steps.body: Save your settings and check that the update takes effect right away on both online checkout and Shopify POS.

steps.heading: Test both checkout and POS
steps.body: Run through a sample online checkout and a POS transaction to make sure the estimated tax no longer appears in either.

faq.question: Can I remove tax for just one region?
faq.answer: Yes, tax settings can be adjusted by region, so you can leave tax active elsewhere while removing it for a specific area.

faq.question: Does this update apply to POS immediately?
faq.answer: Yes, according to the guide, changes to tax settings apply instantly to both checkout and POS once saved.

faq.question: Is this different from the general Shopify tax settings?
faq.answer: It uses the same settings area, but this guide focuses specifically on turning tax off entirely for stores that don't need to collect it.

faq.question: Will this affect existing orders?
faq.answer: No, changing tax settings going forward doesn't retroactively change tax already applied to completed orders.
